summary: Alexander O. Hsu is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago Divinity School (~2011–2018) under supervisors Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later held a teaching position at North Dakota State University (~2019).

Alexander Piatigorsky (1929–2009) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Moscow State University (~1946–1951), he held positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and SOAS University of London, where he was Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia (1990–2001).
Alexander Rogers (1825–1910) was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at East India Company College (~1842–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1845 to 1878.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, supervised by Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He was affiliated with the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972) and served as a professor at Paris Nanterre University from ~1975 to 1991.

Alexander Wynne (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol and earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2000–2003) under doctoral supervisor Richard Gombrich.
Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and completed research under the supervision of Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017).

Alexander von Humboldt (1769–1859) studied at European University Viadrina, the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and the University of Jena (~1794–1797), where he also held a post.

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen (attested 1995) and held posts at Leipzig University (attested 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2011–2013).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein (1877–1937) was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his dissertation under Richard Pischel at Halle (~1898–1900), held a chair at Peking University (1918–1929), and directed the Harvard Sino-Indian Institute (~1928–1937).

Alexandra David-Néel (1868–1969) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels (~1888–1890) and studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1889–1894) and Kazi Dawa Samdup (1912).
Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology and archaeology. She studied under Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Y. Sondaar.

Alexandre Langlois (1788–1854) was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1814–1832). He taught at the Lycée Charlemagne and served as an inspector for the Académie de Paris and member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

Alexis Sanderson (born 1948) is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (1968–1971) and Swami Lakshman Joo (1972), later serving at the University of Oxford as Lecturer (~1977–1992) and Professor (~1992–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel (1942–2023) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his degrees from Haverford College and the University of Chicago (~1964–1973), then spent his career at George Washington University, becoming Columbian Professor in 1981.
Alf Sommerfelt (1892–1965) was a linguist who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924 and served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfonsa Ferrari (1918–1954) was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1939–1943) under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi, continuing there in post-graduate research from ~1943 to 1954.

Alfred Bloom (1926–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1957–1963). He served as professor of religion at the University of Hawaiʻi (1970–1986) and Dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1986–1994).
Alfred Chilton Pearson (1861–1935) was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, entering in 1879, where he was taught by John Peile (~1879–1883).

Alfred Cooper Woolner (1878–1936) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Trinity College, Oxford (~1897–1901). He served as Principal of Oriental College (~1903–1928) and Vice Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (1928–1936).
